macro.headline: Tape softening under the surface; rotation alive in healthcare and travel, tech wobbling.
macro.story:
Start with what the tape actually shows. SPY closed at 728.99, down 0.72% on the day and 2.38% over five sessions, sitting below its 50-day but still 6.1% above its 200-day — sideways trend, RSI 44, MACD negative. QQQ fared worse (-4.5% over 5 days, RSI 47, MACD negative) while the Dow (+0.6% in 5d, RSI 61) and Russell 2000 (+1.0% in 5d, RSI 62) held firm above their 50-day moving averages. VIX rose 12.3% over five days to 18.4, the dollar is firm with DXY RSI at 71, gold is down 7.9% over 21 days and silver down 20%, while WTI crude has collapsed 21.9% over the same window to the high $60s with RSI at 27. S&P 500 breadth reads 57% bullish vs 25% bearish; 8 of 11 GICS sectors sit above their 50-day. None of this is washed out, and none of it is euphoric — it's a tape rotating beneath a flat-to-down headline index.

The causal layer comes from the tracked conversation, which leans net bullish roughly 3-to-1 (three bullish stances, one bearish, one neutral across the tracked voices), but the bearish camp is the loudest single block of posts and centers on Nasdaq volatility and broad-tape risk (SPY, VXN, RSP). The dominant view in today's tracked sentiment attributes the headline weakness to a historically wide gap between Nasdaq-100 volatility and broad market volatility — a tech-specific stress signal — combined with end-of-Q2 positioning, the US reaction to Strait of Hormuz strikes, and a heavy macro week (JOLTS, consumer confidence, ISM, jobs report). A secondary thread in the tracked conversation flags retail rotating out of gold and Bitcoin into semiconductors as a structural rotation theme. This is consistent with what the data shows in two ways — the tech-specific weakness (QQQ -4.5% / 5d while Dow is up) and the gold/silver collapse alongside a firm DXY both line up — but it conflicts with the rotation narrative on one count: the sector data shows leadership in Healthcare, Real Estate, Financials, Industrials, Utilities and small caps, not semis. The tracked rotation narrative may be lagging the actual rotation print.

Underneath the index, the rotation is healthy and broad-defensive-cyclical, not narrow-tech. Healthcare is HOT with RSI 71, Real Estate, Financials, Industrials, Utilities and the Russell 2000 are all HOT with bullish MACD. Technology and the Nasdaq 100 are NEUTRAL/WEAK with bearish MACD, Communication Services is bearish (RSI 28.8), Energy is bearish (RSI 37) consistent with crude's washout, and Consumer Discretionary is bearish at the headline ETF level — yet inside Discretionary, Travel Services is the single highest-scoring Early-Runway industry on the rotation radar. The validated Early-Runway rotation tailwind is firing in Travel Services, Diagnostics & Research, Credit Services, Drug Manufacturers (Spec/Generic), Staffing, Resorts & Casinos and Health Information Services — that's where the hunt is.

Forward watch: this week's calendar (JOLTS Tue, consumer confidence, ISM, jobs report) plus Q2 earnings start give the tape catalysts in both directions. With VIX 18.4 and rising, MACD negative across SPY/QQQ/Nasdaq, but breadth still 57% bullish and most sectors above their 50-day, the honest read is mixed — no validated market-timing signal is active. Engine C is CALM (RSI 44, no washout); the validated washout combo is not in play. Trade the rotation that is actually printing, not the one sentiment is talking about. Confidence is capped at MEDIUM given the MACD/VIX conflict against still-constructive breadth.

Energy equities (XLE, E&P names) face near-term margin compression from lower realized prices, but the broader equity market benefits. Transports and consumer discretionary are direct fuel-cost beneficiaries.
